answer: Each agent key must upload a 10-minute raw GNSS log (pseudorange, carrier phase, Galileo OSNMA-signed nav bits) from its own antenna at a random requested time, so the receiver acts like a quill signing where it sits. Fixes are solved against nearby CORS stations; keys within 50 m merge into one seat, even behind one cedar fence. Each alias needs its own site plus a ~$150 receiver, so N fakes cost N leased sites. A server rack posing as a distant oasis farm fails: simulated signals lack valid OSNMA tags and miss the ionospheric delay the nearest CORS station measured.
